subject: Re: NovusHealth - Exhibit C: Minimum Fee / Cap carveouts (redlines)
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@novushealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Novus Legal <legal@novushealth.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exhibit C clarifications + redline request

Connor —

Thanks for the call this morning. As discussed, our procurement and legal teams reviewed Exhibit C and have two areas we'd like Redwood to consider amending before we proceed to signature:

1) Fee floor interaction with the annualized commit true-up — Novus needs clearer language that the floor will not be applied in months where usage is below the de minimis threshold during the quarter.
2) Pricing cap carveout for burst credits — we request an explicit carveout for one-time burst credits purchased through the Console that shouldn't count toward the annual cap.

I attached a Word doc with inline redlines from our commercial counsel. Can you confirm whether Redwood is amenable to: (a) a narrow definition for the "applicable floor", and (b) a parenthetical exclusion for Console burst credits under the cap?

We have a May 31 target to finalize Exhibit C for the SOW execution. If legal wants to converse directly, loop us in.

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Helen
Helen Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing | NovusHealth
helen.park@novushealth.com

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit C clarifications + redline request

Hi Helen —

Thanks for the redlines and the clear callouts. We've reviewed the attachment at a high level and have a proposed approach:

- Floor interaction: Redwood is open to clarifying the "applicable floor" but prefers to keep the mechanism tied to quarterly true-ups vs month-by-month carveouts. We can propose language that excludes months where Novus's usage is below the stated de minimis (example wording below).
- Burst credits: We can accept an explicit parenthetical that excludes one-time Console burst credits from the annual cap, provided the carveout is limited to purchases tagged as "burst_credit" in our billing metadata (to avoid manipulation).

I'll loop in our pricing lead Marissa and Ben from Legal to draft defensible redline language. Expect an internal note within 24 hours and a redline back to you by EOD Thursday (May 27). If Novus Legal wants to jump on a 30-minute call Thursday morning that helps speed the finish.

Proposed short snippet (working):
"For the avoidance of doubt, months during which Customer usage falls below the de minimis threshold specified in Schedule A shall be excluded from application of the Minimum Fee for purposes of the quarterly true-up."

Can Marissa/Ben you take point on drafting a tighter exhibit redline that captures the above and adds the billing-metadata constraint for burst credits?

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Exhibit C clarifications + redline request — internal draft

Connor / Ben —

Draft attached (see summary below). Kept the change narrow to reduce legal exposure and retained Redwood's right to apply the floor at the quarterly true-up level. Key points:

- Narrow definition for "applicable floor" — tie to Schedule A de minimis and only exclude months explicitly flagged in billing. (Risk: auditor disputes)
- Burst credit carveout — explicit parenthetical that excludes purchases with billing tag "burst_credit"; require documentation within 30 days. (Risk: potential gaming — can be audited)
- Added a short audit clause: Redwood may request supporting billing records within 45 days of invoice to validate carveouts.

Redline snippet included in attachment: pricing_redline_draft.pdf. My recommended negotiation posture for sales: concede the parenthetical for burst credits but retain the billing metadata and audit language. For the floor, accept the exclusion for de minimis months but insist it be implemented only at quarterly true-up (not monthly).

Ben — pls review and flag anything legal thinks is a material concession. If we sign off I will convert to tracked Word and send to Helen.

Marissa Cole
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
attachment: pricing_redline_draft.pdf (pdf)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@novushealth.com>
Cc: Novus Legal <legal@novushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Exhibit C clarifications + redline request

Helen —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's proposed Exhibit C with tracked changes (see attached Novus_OrderForm_ExhibitC_redline.docx). Summary of our agreed positions and proposed language:

1) Floor interaction with quarterly true-up
- Proposed language: "For avoidance of doubt, months during which Customer usage is below the de minimis threshold set forth in Schedule A shall not be counted toward application of the Minimum Fee for the purposes of the Quarterly True-Up. The Minimum Fee shall continue to be calculated and applied at the Quarterly True-Up level in accordance with Section 3.2."

2) Burst credit carveout
- Proposed language: "The Annual Pricing Cap shall exclude one-time Console 'burst' credits that are identified in Redwood's billing system with the tag 'burst_credit' and for which Customer provides documentation within thirty (30) days of purchase. Redwood reserves the right to validate such purchases and, if inconsistent with the tag or documentation, to treat them as billable usage for cap calculations."

3) Audit and documentation
- Proposed: Redwood may request supporting billing records and may audit documented burst purchases within forty-five (45) days after invoice to confirm applicability of exclusions.

We believe this preserves the commercial intent Novus outlined while protecting Redwood against manipulation. If Novus Legal is comfortable with the documentation and audit language, we can finalize Exhibit C and move to SOW execution.

Next steps:
- If these redlines are acceptable, Helen, confirm and I'll upload the tracked Word to the HubSpot deal and start the DocuSign envelope.
- If Novus Legal wants a short call to finalize wording, Marissa and Ben are available Monday morning (May 31).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
